notes_for_editor: Roster from USLHS archive page (cite 10): 71 lines, 1893-1974; the archive lists no head keeper 1944-1949. The keepers array is built from that page's lines. Sources disagree on: Clark 1911 accident (HistoryLink: Blaine, jumped to fetch a rowboat; LighthouseFriends: Semiahmoo, swam for help); fog-signal building 1893 vs 1898; tower height; who demolished buildings (BLM contract per Parks vs 1985 Coast Guard reservists per KOPL); fate of the original lens (NRHP 1977 says on display at Admiralty Head; LF says Jim Gibbs; KOPL says Fresnel still in tower in 1985). Wikipedia not used. The 1925 Bulletin text is column-interleaved, so the 14 October rescue was read by position; the boat name and the year of the event are not given on the page, and the Bulletin index lists the item at p. 110 of the 1924-29 index. 1891-92 and 1893-94 reports cited by volume and entry number, not printed page (OCR page labels unconfirmed). LHB 1900 trumpet engine size in OCR is '1^ horsepower'. Lighthouse Board 1888 recommendation read second-hand via LighthouseFriends; its currents quote describes the Canadian East Point, not Patos. The 1912 Colonist account is second-hand via LighthouseFriends. Modern (post-1960) keepers are listed in the roster only as the archive prints them. 1977 NRHP nomination calls the daughter 'Helen Slidden' (OCR/typo) for Helene Durgan Glidden.
